statement: The true Weil quadratic form on smooth functions supported in an interval of length 1/1024 has lower bound (2/5)||f||². Every fixed bounded window has a closed semibounded realization, but a translated pair separated by log 2 has a strictly negative cross term; local direct-sum positivity cannot be presumed.
hypotheses: Classical unconditional Weil explicit formula on compactly supported smooth functions, standard Fourier convention and digamma series.
definitions: Q=sum over completed xi zero divisor of q(z) conjugate(q(conjugate(z))); arithmetic formula with poles, digamma multiplier, prime-power shifts.
source_locators: Suzuki, Aspects of the screw function, doi:10.1112/jlms.12785 eq. 5.15; NIST DLMF 5.4, 5.7, 5.11; Connes-Consani arXiv:2006.13771; Suzuki arXiv:2606.09096.
proof_or_gap: Plancherel and explicit digamma bounds give uniform tiny-window coercivity without zeros as inputs; a bounded pole/prime perturbation of the weighted Fourier form yields fixed-window self-adjoint realizations. The prime shift at log 2 produces a cross term bounded above by (-1/4+6L)||f||². A Schur complement condition identifies the missing gluing inequality.
implication_to_claim: A rigorous scoped step on the genuine arithmetic form, not a synthetic spectrum; global positivity and spectral correspondence are not proved.
unproved_dependencies: Control of cross-window interactions for arbitrary supports, no uniform positive floor asserted globally; a noncircular spectral correspondence with multiplicities and complex zero mapping.
adversarial_findings: Prior small-support positivity is substantially stronger than this elementary bound. Cross-term negativity does not imply a negative full form or disprove RH.
